questions.article: The End of History Is Near
questions.q: Scientists now warn, on the basis of data, that the earth’s time is limited. With whose earlier message does the article compare this?
options: The ancient philosophers of Greece
Not quite. The article says: The prophets, who warned that this world will end and each person will answer for his deeds.
The prophets, who warned that this world will end and each person will answer for his deeds
Yes. The Quran calls them Nazeer – those who warn.
The rulers of ancient Egypt
Not quite. The article says: The prophets, who warned that this world will end and each person will answer for his deeds.
The poets of Arabia
Not quite. The article says: The prophets, who warned that this world will end and each person will answer for his deeds.
questions.rationale: “Previous warnings were given on the basis of divine revelation. The scientific community is giving the same warning on the basis of scientific data. The time for introspection has come.”

questions.q: The lion cannot tell its side of the story. In what way, according to the article, is truth like the lion in this world?
options: It is admired only from a distance
Not quite. The article says: It does not speak for itself now, but a time will come when reality is made plain to all.
It lives far from human society
Not quite. The article says: It does not speak for itself now, but a time will come when reality is made plain to all.
It does not speak for itself now, but a time will come when reality is made plain to all
Well read. The present state is temporary.
It is fierce and frightens people
Not quite. The article says: It does not speak for itself now, but a time will come when reality is made plain to all.
questions.rationale: “In the midst of this verbal uproar, truth remains concealed—truth does not speak of itself… A time is sure to come when the lion speaks.”

questions.q: In a study of ninety leaders, many spoke of “false starts” but never of “failure.” What does this reveal about them?
options: They never actually met with setbacks
Not quite. The article says: They treat a setback as a hurdle and turn disappointment into greater resolve and a better approach.
They hid their mistakes from others
Not quite. The article says: They treat a setback as a hurdle and turn disappointment into greater resolve and a better approach.
They depended on unusual talent
Not quite. The article says: They treat a setback as a hurdle and turn disappointment into greater resolve and a better approach.
They treat a setback as a hurdle and turn disappointment into greater resolve and a better approach
Right. They always have another idea to test.
questions.rationale: “Disappointment spawns greater resolve, growth or change… super-achievers always feel there are other avenues they can explore.”

questions.q: According to the article, peak performance is very often less a matter of adding new knowledge than of what?
options: Copying the methods of rivals
Not quite. The article says: Developing capacities one already has but is barely aware of.
Finding influential friends
Not quite. The article says: Developing capacities one already has but is barely aware of.
Developing capacities one already has but is barely aware of
Yes. A sense of mission taps these hidden resources.
Waiting for the right time
Not quite. The article says: Developing capacities one already has but is barely aware of.
questions.rationale: “It is not so much a question of adding to one’s knowledge and skills as of developing what is already there—capacities of which we are sometimes barely aware.”

questions.q: “Those who turn away from everything vain” (23:3). What practical rule does the article draw from this?
options: Avoid all conversation
Not quite. The article says: Weigh the likely result before acting, and refrain from what will yield nothing or prove counter-productive.
Do only what brings quick profit
Not quite. The article says: Weigh the likely result before acting, and refrain from what will yield nothing or prove counter-productive.
Weigh the likely result before acting, and refrain from what will yield nothing or prove counter-productive
Correct. Life is too short to waste.
Act first and reflect afterwards
Not quite. The article says: Weigh the likely result before acting, and refrain from what will yield nothing or prove counter-productive.
questions.rationale: “Before taking any action, the believer must assess its possible result… If there is any possibility that your step will prove to be counter-productive, then refrain from taking it.”

questions.q: How does the article distinguish spirituality from ecstasy?
options: Spirituality is a deeper kind of trance
Not quite. The article says: Spirituality is a state of keen intellectual awakening, not a trance that blurs the mind.
Spirituality is a state of keen intellectual awakening, not a trance that blurs the mind
Right. It belongs with contemplation.
Spirituality is only for those who live in forests
Not quite. The article says: Spirituality is a state of keen intellectual awakening, not a trance that blurs the mind.
Spirituality means giving up thinking
Not quite. The article says: Spirituality is a state of keen intellectual awakening, not a trance that blurs the mind.
questions.rationale: “Spirituality is very different from this, being marked by a high level of acute intellectual awakening, rather than a semi-somnolent state of mind.”

questions.q: What does the honey bee teach the “awakened mind”?
options: To work in large groups
Not quite. The article says: To draw spiritual nourishment from everything, as the bee takes only nectar and wastes no time on other things.
To store up food for hard times
Not quite. The article says: To draw spiritual nourishment from everything, as the bee takes only nectar and wastes no time on other things.
To draw spiritual nourishment from everything, as the bee takes only nectar and wastes no time on other things
Well reasoned. The whole world becomes a garden.
To keep away from human beings
Not quite. The article says: To draw spiritual nourishment from everything, as the bee takes only nectar and wastes no time on other things.
questions.rationale: “For an awakened mind, the whole world is a world of spirituality. It extracts spiritual content from everything.”

questions.q: Father Heras held a degree in Spanish history, yet offered to teach Indian history, of which he then knew nothing. What does the article admire in this?
options: He was ordered to do so by the principal
Not quite. The article says: With a great purpose before him, no task seemed too hard – he studied until he became a historian of repute.
With a great purpose before him, no task seemed too hard – he studied until he became a historian of repute
Yes. A mission makes hardship light.
He thought Indian history a small subject
Not quite. The article says: With a great purpose before him, no task seemed too hard – he studied until he became a historian of repute.
He wished to avoid hard work
Not quite. The article says: With a great purpose before him, no task seemed too hard – he studied until he became a historian of repute.
questions.rationale: “It is when one has a great and over-riding mission in life that no task seems too difficult, no hardship too great.”

questions.q: The article likens insincere behaviour to flowing water. Why?
options: Because it is pure and refreshing
Not quite. The article says: Its course is decided by the ground it meets – the insincere person simply yields to each situation’s interest.
Because it always finds the sea
Not quite. The article says: Its course is decided by the ground it meets – the insincere person simply yields to each situation’s interest.
Because it is strong and unstoppable
Not quite. The article says: Its course is decided by the ground it meets – the insincere person simply yields to each situation’s interest.
Its course is decided by the ground it meets – the insincere person simply yields to each situation’s interest
Exactly. Sincerity asks one to think and choose by principle.
questions.rationale: “This kind of behaviour is like that of flowing water. The contours of the surface of the earth determine its path. The one who is insincere is always ready to accede to the demands of a given situation.”

questions.q: What, according to the article, gives death its gravity?
options: It ends all a person’s plans
Not quite. The article says: It is not the end of life but the beginning of an eternal life of reward or retribution.
It is painful to those left behind
Not quite. The article says: It is not the end of life but the beginning of an eternal life of reward or retribution.
It is not the end of life but the beginning of an eternal life of reward or retribution
Yes. Only what has worth in the after-life will remain.
It comes only in old age
Not quite. The article says: It is not the end of life but the beginning of an eternal life of reward or retribution.
questions.rationale: “The gravity of the situation lies in death not being the end of life, but rather the beginning of a new, eternal life.”
